title: Choose a transcription method · Level 3
slo: Choose real-time or batch transcription for a workplace audio task.

exercises.question_text: How are batch transcription jobs scheduled?

options.rationale: Batch jobs use a best-effort schedule. They commonly begin within minutes, but no running time is guaranteed.

options.error_type: Confuses best-effort scheduling with guaranteed timing
options.rationale: Batch job timing is not guaranteed. A job may begin within minutes but does not change to running at a promised time.
options.better_fit: A guaranteed time would fit a situation where timing is explicitly promised.

feedback.intrinsic: A deadline could be set based on a time that is not promised.
feedback.instructional: Treat batch timing as best-effort rather than guaranteed.

options.error_type: Confuses batch jobs with real-time transcription
options.rationale: Transcription during speech is real-time transcription. Batch jobs process stored recordings later.
options.better_fit: Use real-time transcription while a person is speaking.

feedback.intrinsic: The team could select a batch job for a live need.
feedback.instructional: Live incoming audio and scheduled batch work are different methods.

options.rationale: Speech synthesis turns text into audible speech. Batch transcription turns stored audio into text.
options.better_fit: Use speech synthesis after text is available and needs to be spoken aloud.

feedback.intrinsic: The schedule question would be confused with creating audio from text.
feedback.instructional: Batch transcription concerns recorded audio and later text results.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Batch jobs use best-effort scheduling, so their exact running time is not guaranteed.

exercises.question_text: Which statements about a SAS URI are correct? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: SAS is the abbreviation for shared access signature. A SAS URI can be used for stored audio.

options.text: It can point to audio in storage
options.rationale: A SAS URI can identify audio files in storage. Batch transcription can use that URI.
Batch transcription can point to stored audio with a SAS URI. This fits recordings held in storage.

options.text: It is a live audio stream
options.error_type: Confuses a storage URI with incoming audio
options.rationale: A SAS URI points to audio files in storage. A live stream is incoming audio used for real-time transcription.
options.better_fit: Use a live audio stream when a person is speaking and text is needed as they speak.

feedback.intrinsic: The recording location would be confused with audio arriving now.
feedback.instructional: A URI identifies stored audio; it is not the audio stream itself.

exercises.explanation: Correct. SAS stands for shared access signature, and its URI can identify stored audio for batch transcription.

exercises.question_text: Real-time transcription can be used when someone is speaking during a presentation.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Captions would arrive too late for people following the presentation.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Real-time transcription is intended for incoming speech, including presentations and demonstrations.

exercises.explanation: Correct. A presentation is a live-speaking situation, so text can be returned as the person speaks.

exercises.question_text: What transcription method is designed for stored audio recordings?

options.rationale: Batch transcription processes stored recordings. Its results are returned asynchronously.

options.error_type: Confuses stored recordings with incoming speech
options.rationale: Real-time transcription is for incoming audio while someone speaks. Stored recordings fit batch transcription.
options.better_fit: Use real-time transcription for a presentation, demonstration, or other live-speaking situation.

feedback.intrinsic: The team would treat an existing recording like live speech.
feedback.instructional: Match stored audio with batch transcription.

options.rationale: Speech synthesis makes audio from text. It does not transcribe an audio recording.
options.better_fit: Use speech synthesis to read text aloud or create an audio file from text.

feedback.intrinsic: The recording would remain without a written transcript.
feedback.instructional: Transcription converts audio to text; synthesis moves in the other direction.

options.rationale: Voice Live supports real-time spoken conversations. It is not the batch workflow for stored recordings.
options.better_fit: Use Voice Live for a conversational voice experience with spoken responses.

feedback.intrinsic: The stored recordings would not be queued for the needed transcription task.
feedback.instructional: For recorded audio that can be processed later, choose batch transcription.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Batch transcription is designed to process recordings that are already stored.

exercises.question_text: A shared access signature (SAS) URI is a storage pointer, not a transcription method.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The task could assign transcription work to a URI that only identifies stored audio.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A SAS URI points batch transcription to stored audio, while the transcription service performs the conversion.

exercises.explanation: Correct. A SAS URI identifies audio in storage for batch transcription; it does not perform transcription.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The processing flow is no longer clear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with the application, then its streamed input, the live context, and the returned text.

exercises.correct_answer: An application streams incoming audio for live transcription then receives text
exercises.explanation: Real-time transcription begins with incoming audio being streamed, then returns text while the audio is live. This emphasizes the application flow rather than merely naming the method.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The stored recording would be treated as if it required live text.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Real-time transcription is for incoming speech; batch transcription fits stored audio and later results.

exercises.explanation: Stored audio does not need to be transcribed as it arrives. Batch transcription processes those recordings and returns results after submission.

exercises.question_text: A video platform needs captions during a live stream. Which choices support the right method? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: A live stream has incoming speech. Real-time transcription returns text as people speak.
Real-time transcription needs incoming audio from a microphone or another input source. A live stream provides that audio.
Live captions require text during the speech. Real-time transcription returns transcribed text from incoming audio.

options.error_type: Confuses immediate captions with asynchronous batch processing
options.rationale: A batch job handles stored recordings and returns results asynchronously. Later scheduling cannot provide captions during the live stream.
options.better_fit: Schedule a batch job to process a saved recording after the stream ends.

feedback.intrinsic: Viewers would miss captions while watching the live stream.
feedback.instructional: Immediate captions require real-time transcription, not later batch processing.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Live captions require incoming audio to be transcribed and returned while people speak.

exercises.question_text: Reconstruct the statement from the pieces.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The sentence no longer clearly connects stored audio with later results.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Place the method first, then its input, followed by the timing of its result.

exercises.correct_answer: Batch transcription processes stored recordings and returns results later
exercises.explanation: The sentence names the method, identifies stored recordings as its input, and states that results arrive later. Those details define batch transcription.

exercises.question_text: A customer support lead needs transcripts for a caller who is speaking now and for stored calls from last month. For the live caller, which choice is best?

options.rationale: The caller is speaking now, so the audio is incoming. Real-time transcription provides text as the call happens.

options.error_type: Confuses live calls with stored recordings
options.rationale: Batch transcription is appropriate for the calls stored from last month. It is not the right choice for the caller speaking now.
options.better_fit: Use batch transcription for the stored calls from last month when results can arrive later.

feedback.intrinsic: The lead would not get a transcript during the live caller’s conversation.
feedback.instructional: Choose based on audio timing: live callers need real-time transcription.

options.error_type: Confuses a storage pointer with a transcription method
options.rationale: A SAS URI can point batch transcription to audio files in storage. It does not transcribe the live caller.
options.better_fit: Use a SAS URI when locating stored calls for batch transcription.

feedback.intrinsic: The live conversation would still have no transcription method selected.
feedback.instructional: A SAS URI identifies stored audio; it is not a choice for live transcription.

options.error_type: Confuses creating transcripts with generating spoken audio
options.rationale: Text-to-speech converts response text into spoken audio. The lead needs speech from the caller converted into text.
options.better_fit: Use text-to-speech when written content needs to be played as audio.

feedback.intrinsic: The caller’s words would not be captured as a transcript.
feedback.instructional: For a transcript, choose speech-to-text through real-time transcription.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The caller is speaking live, so real-time transcription is the best choice.

exercises.question_text: A shared access signature is also called a ___.

parts.text: A shared access signature is also called a

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The stored audio would not be identified by the correct URI term.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The storage pointer is a SAS URI; a batch method processes recordings, while endpoints and keys support connection and authentication.

exercises.explanation: SAS is the abbreviation for shared access signature, and the URI can point batch transcription to stored audio. Batch transcription, endpoints, and keys have different roles.

exercises.question_text: Which statements describe batch job scheduling? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Batch jobs are scheduled on a best-effort basis. Their start timing is not guaranteed.
A batch job normally starts within minutes after the request. This is common timing, not a promise.
There is no guaranteed time when the job changes to running. Best-effort scheduling allows that uncertainty.

options.error_type: Confuses batch scheduling with real-time transcription
options.rationale: Text during live speech describes real-time transcription. Batch jobs process stored recordings on a best-effort schedule.
options.better_fit: Expect text during speech when using real-time transcription.

feedback.intrinsic: A producer could promise live results that a batch job does not provide.
feedback.instructional: Batch scheduling concerns later processing, not transcription while someone speaks.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Batch jobs are best-effort: they commonly start within minutes, but the running time is not guaranteed.
